approach:
Keep `Athena::retry`, `ask`, `queue` and `first_reading` behaving exactly as now, because the automatic drain calls `retry` (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:4635). Each becomes a thin wrapper over a private inner function that takes an optional hand guard (None = today's code path, with the same `commit_records` call). Three new public entry points, `retry_by_hand(job, force, ui)`, `ask_by_hand(text, force, ui)` and `queue_by_hand(text, force)`, build one shared `HandGuard` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and call the same inner functions.

The guard blocks in three cases, tested in this order for each job it covers (the named job, plus the job `retry_target` resolves to, reading.rs:1304):
1. An interrupted job that was already retried. This is the refusal `retry` has had since reading.rs:1288. Only `retry_by_hand` counts it, so `--force` can pass it.
2. A retry linked to the job that is Queued, Proposed, Blocked or Dispatched. A new `live_retry_of` scans `job_history` for it.
3. Athena's failure review of the job is pending, via a new `failure_review_pending` in introspect.rs. It is true only when a review is really outstanding: a deferred queue file exists, only kill-switch failures are recorded, or the outcome is younger than the review's own time limit (`reader_timeout_s`, introspect.rs:1965). An old job whose review will never be written is not pending, so it retries as before.

The guard runs twice. The first run is before any model call and returns the cheap refusal. The second is inside the `commit_records_with` closure (commits.rs:246-276). That closure runs under the repository lock and runs again whenever the branch moved. It re-reads the records at the head being committed. This closes the window in which the drain's retry, or another hand retry, commits while this hand reader is still running.

With `--force` the guard lets the retry through. The `Intervention` (category OverrodeDecision, source Observed, job = the retried job) goes in the same commit as the new request, reading and invocation. The trailers are `Athena-Job` and `Athena-Intervention`, as in `correct` (reading.rs:1453-1456). After the commit, `introspect_intervention` runs, as `correct` does (reading.rs:1464).

`--force` is added to `Command::Retry` and `Command::Ask`. `athena status` gets a new `failure_note` field on `JobLine` only (not `JobTrace`). It reads 'failure review pending', or 'retry <id> queued', 'retry <id> running' or 'retry <id> interrupted'. README.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated.

decisions.choice: Hand-only entry points over shared inner functions; the automatic path keeps its current code. One private `HandGuard` (force, covered jobs, interrupted flag, review limit, planned override) with `settle_hand` for the first check and `commit_hand` for the guarded commit. `first_reading` stays as a wrapper over `first_reading_with(.., guard)`. That function needs `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`, as `read_for` has at reading.rs:523, because it grows to 8 parameters.
decisions.reason: Athena::retry is also the automatic path: drain.rs:4635 (`ReadOf::Retry`) calls it, drain.rs:1972-1981 chooses it after a failed attempt, and steward.rs:450 (`interrupted_work`) reads `retried_job`. About 70 tests call `retry` and `ask` directly, and `a_rejected_job_can_be_retried_twice` (tests/retry.rs:1282) calls `retry` twice in a row. A guard inside `retry` would change automatic behavior and break them. `read_queued` (reading.rs:1170) and `read_unread` (:1185) call `first_reading` and keep working. Hand commands that queue a retry, re-ask or follow-up are `athena retry`, `athena ask` and `athena ask --later` with 'try again on <job>' text (RETRY_PREFIX is built at reading.rs:1319; users type the same text). `accept-proposal` (proposals.rs:643) and `approve-work` ask for new work. `correct` (reading.rs:1336) accepts only Proposed or Declined jobs. Criterion 6 is met: `hand_blocker`, `settle_hand` and `commit_hand` each have one definition in reading.rs, and all three entry points call them.

rejected.option: Put the guard inside `Athena::retry` with a `force` parameter
rejected.why: It changes the drain's retry and breaks about 70 callers.

rejected.option: Copy the check into each command in commands.rs
rejected.why: Criterion 6 needs one shared path in reading.rs.

decisions.choice: A retry stands (queued or running) when its state is Queued, Proposed, Blocked or Dispatched. The newest such retry is found by scanning `job_history(records)` for `retry_of == job`. Dispatched counts whether or not a process is alive; the refusal text uses `retry_follow_up(records, id, self.running(id))`.
decisions.reason: `retry_follow_up` (reading/retry.rs:272-293) already maps Queued, Proposed and Blocked to 'run athena go', Dispatched-running to 'wait' and Dispatched-not-running to 'interrupted too'. `retries_by_job` (retry.rs:246-268) keeps only the newest retry and counts Failed and Landed retries, so a newer failed retry would hide an older queued one. A retry that ended Failed, was Dropped, Declined, Abandoned, Stale or Closed does not stand, so retrying again stays allowed (existing test `a_dropped_retry_does_not_block_a_new_retry`, tests/retry.rs:1217). `job_history` reads the request form through `retried_job` and `retry_reference` (retry.rs:560-580), so the guard accepts exactly the forms `ask` accepts.

rejected.why: It counts ended retries and keeps only the newest.

decisions.choice: `failure_review_pending` is a pure function in introspect.rs: `(records, job, now, limit_s, deferred: &dyn Fn(&JobId) -> bool) -> bool`. An `Athena` method supplies `now = crate::now()`, `limit_s = reader_timeout_s` from `JobConfig::at(head)`, and `deferred` = the file `<introspect_pending_dir>/job-<id>.json` exists. It returns false unless the job's state is Closed(Rejected or Failed), the same set as `event_of_job` (introspect.rs:1546-1550). Then: (a) a Rejection or Failure introspection of the job that is Recorded, or Failed for a reason other than the kill switch, means settled, so false. (b) Otherwise, a record that failed on KILL_SWITCH_TEXT (introspect.rs:820) means pending. (c) A deferred queue file means pending. (d) `now - outcome.at < limit_s` seconds means the review may still be running, so pending. (e) Anything else is false.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 4. The literal rule, 'no review record', would make every old rejected or failed job whose review was never written need `--force` for ever. That breaks 'works as before' (criterion 3). Such jobs are common: jobs from before reviews existed, and jobs where `introspect` returned an error before writing a record (head, load, read_records, JobConfig, redactor and scratch-dir errors at introspect.rs:1610-1628 are only printed by `settle`, :1524-1535). Nothing in the code will ever write those reviews. A review can still be running only for as long as its model call may last, and that call is bounded by `reader_timeout_s` (introspect.rs:1965; live athena.toml:50 sets 86400). So a review is 'still pending' only while one of three things is true. First, the review is deferred by the kill switch (introspect.rs:1389-1405); `athena start` runs it. Second, only kill-switch failures exist; `requeue_kill_switch_failures` (:1436-1492) requeues them. Third, the outcome is younger than that bound. A failed review for another reason is final (introspect.rs:1495-1496). This also covers the short window between the outcome commit and the review commit (run/mod.rs:431-437) that a pure records check would miss. The rule lives next to `KILL_SWITCH_TEXT`, which is a private const, and `event_key`, so those are not copied. For old jobs, after `reader_timeout_s` the refusal stops and `athena retry` works without `--force`; the text names `--force` and `athena start` as the ways out while it applies.

rejected.option: Records-only rule: no review record means pending, for ever
rejected.why: Old jobs and jobs whose review errored early would need `--force` for ever, and criterion 3 'works as before' fails for them.

rejected.option: Only the pending-queue file means pending
rejected.why: It misses the minutes between the outcome commit and the review commit.

rejected.option: Add a new registry entry while the review runs
rejected.why: It changes the automatic path (go_with_stages, run/mod.rs:431-437), which must not change.

decisions.choice: The guard re-checks inside the commit. `first_reading_with` and `queue_inner` call `commit_hand`, which calls `commit_records_with(&|head| guard.files_at(self, head, &files), &message)`. `files_at` loads `Records::load(&self.git, head)` and runs `hand_blocker` again. Without `--force` and with a blocker it returns Err, which `commit_records_in` propagates at commits.rs:264 before `build_commit_in`, so nothing is committed. The Err names the retry that won.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 3. The drain retries a failed item right after `go` (drain.rs:1972-1981, `run_job` :1645 `self.steps.read(from)`, `Athena::retry` at :4635). `go_with_stages` writes the review first (run/mod.rs:431-437). The retry job is committed only after the reader finishes (reading.rs:1216-1253), which takes minutes. During that read there is a review record and no retry record, so a first check alone passes a hand retry and both proposals land: the 'closed as a duplicate, 2 jobs' failure. The closure runs under `lock_repository` (commits.rs:261) and runs again whenever the branch moved (:262-268), so the check and the commit are atomic against any other Athena process. If the hand retry commits first, the drain's `retry` (unchanged by this job) can still add a copy; that is a stated limit in CHANGELOG.md, since the automatic path must not change. The refused read's model spend is not recorded, as for any failed commit (the gate refusal at commits.rs:203-213 has the same effect). The Err says the reading was discarded.

rejected.option: Check only before the reader runs
rejected.why: It cannot see a retry committed while the reader runs.

rejected.option: Commit the refused read as a Queued job so the cost is recorded
rejected.why: It would create another 'try again on' job that the drain would read: another duplicate.

rejected.option: Change the drain to mark the failed job in flight
rejected.why: It changes automatic retry behavior, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: The forced override is written atomically with the retry. `settle_hand` builds the `Intervention` when `--force` meets a blocker: new id (checked with `has_record_id`), category OverrodeDecision, source Observed, job = the retried job, class_of_work = `job.class()` or 'unknown' (as `event_of_job`, introspect.rs:1555), `what` naming the retry and its state or the pending review, `why` = the user chose a second retry over Athena's own. `commit_hand` adds that file to the same commit as the request, invocation and reading, with trailers `Athena-Job: <new job>` and `Athena-Intervention: <id>` (the gate needs the trailer for a commit that adds an intervention, athena-gate/src/invariant.rs:23 and :799-800; `correct` does the same at reading.rs:1453-1456). After the commit it calls `introspect_intervention(&id, ui)`, as `correct` does at reading.rs:1464, because 'every intervention is introspected at once' (manage.rs:399). That call never fails the command. `--force` with nothing blocking at the first check writes no intervention.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 5 and removes the old plan's gap between the retry commit and the intervention commit: one commit holds both, so no interrupt can leave a forced retry without its intervention. `InterventionSource::Observed` is 'Captured by Athena itself' (athena-data records.rs:231-233), and `correct` records a user's act the same way. `User` would list it as open work in `athena status` (status.rs:552-556) and the score reads only User interventions. A failed job's closing score is not touched: `expected_score` counts only interventions with `at <= score time` (athena-gate/src/jobs.rs:122-130), and only `athena intervene` writes re-scores (manage.rs:365-375). No signal or rule reads OverrodeDecision (only athena-data records.rs:152-178 and docs mention it), and no new record kind is added, so no athena-data change is needed.

rejected.option: Commit the intervention in a second commit after the retry
rejected.why: An interrupt between the two leaves a forced retry with no intervention; the plan had to state that as a limit.

rejected.option: Skip introspection of the forced override
rejected.why: manage.rs:399 and `correct` introspect every intervention; skipping needs a recorded exception.
It would show as open work in status and would re-score the closed job.
It needs an athena-data allow-list change for no gain.

decisions.choice: Status adds `failure_note: Option<String>` (skip when None) to `JobLine` only; `JobTrace` is not changed. A private `Athena::failure_note(records, job, limit_s)` applies to jobs Closed(Rejected, Failed, TimedOut or Stale). It gives 'retry <id> queued' (Queued, Proposed or Blocked), 'retry <id> running' (Dispatched with a registry entry) or 'retry <id> interrupted' (Dispatched without one), from `live_retry_of`. Otherwise it gives 'failure review pending' when `failure_review_pending` holds. A pure helper `failure_note_text(live, pending)` takes those inputs, so it is unit-tested without a repository. `scan_jobs` (status.rs:1115) fills it in. `plan_suffix` (display.rs:1060-1083) shows it as ` · <note>`.
decisions.reason: The brief says no existing field is reused. `JobLine.retried_as` is documented (status.rs:100-103) as 'The id of the retry that stands for this job, for an interrupted job that was already retried'. It feeds the interrupted next-line text (status.rs:1166-1177), and widening it would change that text. Only `status` (the `recent` list) is asked for, so the trace is left alone, which also leaves the JobTrace fixture at display.rs:2105 untouched. `athena status` reads the worktree records (status.rs:1194-1195), while hand commands read HEAD; they are the same commit in normal use.

rejected.why: It would change its documented meaning and the interrupted next-line text.

rejected.option: Also add the note to JobTrace
rejected.why: Not asked for; it widens the diff and the display.

decisions.choice: Files outside the brief's expected list, answering findings 1, 2 and 7: crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs and README.md are added. crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs and crates/athena-data/src/records/core.rs, listed by the brief, are not edited.
decisions.reason: introspect.rs: the pending rule must read the private const `KILL_SWITCH_TEXT` (introspect.rs:820) and `event_key` (:824), the single definition of which events are reviewed. Copying them into reading.rs, already 396510 bytes, would duplicate a string that must match. Only one function and one small method are added there. display.rs: the new `JobLine` field has to be shown, and two tests build `JobLine` by literal (display.rs:2679 and :2770) and would not compile without it. The brief says no existing field is reused, so a new field is required. README.md: the command table at README.md:80-81 documents `athena ask` and `athena retry <job> [--yes]`, so it gains `--force` and one sentence on the refusal. Tests that read README.md look only for unrelated needles (main.rs:1637-1656, xtask/tests/site_page.rs:213-214). steward.rs stays untouched: the brief's Out of scope says automatic retry (drain, steward) does not change, and steward.rs:450 only reads `retried_job`. `Intervention` is defined at athena-data/src/records.rs:1066, not in records/core.rs (which holds decision records), and no new kind is needed.

rejected.option: Reuse an existing JobLine field so display.rs stays untouched
rejected.why: Every candidate field has another documented meaning.

decisions.choice: Exit table for the new and changed stages. (a) Refused at the first check, no `--force`: `settle_hand` in reading.rs returns Err before any model call and before `refuse_if_stopped` is reached in `ask`. No commit and no job. The message names the standing retry's id, its state and the `retry_follow_up` text, or says 'the failure review of job <id> is pending', and in every case 'Nothing was queued'; it offers `--force`. The CLI prints the error and exits non-zero. The next reader of state is `athena status`, which shows `failure_note`. (b) `--force` over a blocker at the first check: the override is planned, the retry is read as usual, and the intervention is committed with it (see the override decision). Records afterwards: a new job and one intervention in one commit; `status::intervention_counts` (status.rs:989) counts it. (c) No blocker, with or without `--force`: the unchanged path runs and writes no intervention. (d) Refused at commit time without `--force` (a retry landed during the read): the `files_at` Err leaves HEAD as the other process left it, with no new job. The reader's spend is not recorded, and the message says the reading was discarded. (e) `--force` and a blocker that appears only at commit time: the retry is committed with no intervention, because no blocker was seen when the user decided; this is stated in CHANGELOG.md. (f) An error loading records, config or the guard's inputs is returned with `?` before anything is committed. (g) Line pause (reading.rs:1280), kill switch / hold (`refuse_if_stopped`, reading.rs:948) and the budget preflight (reading.rs:1315) keep their order and text; the guard sits after the pause check and before `ask`. (h) Interrupt before the commit leaves nothing. Interrupt after the commit leaves the retry and its intervention together, and only the post-commit introspection can be missing, which never blocks (as for `correct`). (i) The commit fails (gate refusal at commits.rs:203-213, or the branch moving 3 times, commits.rs:275): Err, no job and no intervention. (j) Automatic callers: the guard is None, so `commit_records` is called exactly as before.
decisions.reason: The brief requires that the exits of a changed flow be listed. Each exit above names the file:line that handles it, the state it leaves and the reader of that state.

files.purpose: Add `live_retry_of`, `Blocker`, `HandGuard`, `hand_blocker`, `settle_hand` (first check, override planning) and `commit_hand` (re-check inside `commit_records_with`, intervention in the same commit, trailers, `introspect_intervention` afterwards). Add public `retry_by_hand`, `ask_by_hand` and `queue_by_hand`. Turn `retry`, `ask`, `queue` and `first_reading` into thin wrappers over `retry_inner`, `ask_inner`, `queue_inner` and `first_reading_with` that take an optional guard. The existing interrupted-job refusal stays for the non-hand path. Update the doc comment of `retry`.

Add the pure `failure_review_pending(records, job, now, limit_s, deferred)` and an `Athena` method that supplies the clock, `reader_timeout_s` and the pending-queue file check. Add unit tests `failure_review_pending_*`. (Not in the brief's list; it needs the private `KILL_SWITCH_TEXT` and `event_key`.)
Add `--force` to `Command::Ask` and `Command::Retry` with help text, pass it in `run`, update the `retry` help text, and add clap tests.
`ask` and `retry` take `force` and call `ask_by_hand`, `queue_by_hand` and `retry_by_hand`; print one line naming the intervention when an override was recorded.

New tests for the acceptance cases (queued, drain race, pending, old job, no-block baseline, forced second retry with intervention, status note, shared guard and input forms, help flags, binary refusal). Add an `athena_bin(&fx)` helper copied from introspection.rs:292. Comment `a_rejected_job_can_be_retried_twice` as the automatic path.
Add `[--force]` and one sentence on the refusal to the `athena ask` and `athena retry` rows of the command table (README.md:80-81).

One bullet under '## [Unreleased]' / '### Changed': the failure, the guard and its first and commit-time checks, the pending rule and its time bound, `--force` with the intervention in the same commit and its introspection, the status note, what is unchanged (drain, steward), the limits, and the tests.

steps: Read-only first: re-read reading.rs:947-1004 (`ask`, `queue`), :1199-1262 (`first_reading`), :1274-1333 (`retry`), commits.rs:246-276, introspect.rs:820-837 and :1538-1579, reading/retry.rs:195-293, status.rs:1115-1155. Edit in the order below so the tree builds at each step.

Step 1, introspect.rs: add `pub fn failure_review_pending(records: &Records, job: &JobRecords, now: Timestamp, limit_s: u64, deferred: &dyn Fn(&JobId) -> bool) -> bool` beside `KILL_SWITCH_TEXT`, with the rule order (state, settled, kill-switch record, deferred file, age under `limit_s`, else false). Compute age as `now.as_second() - outcome.at.as_second()`. Add `impl Athena { pub fn failure_review_pending(&self, records, job, limit_s) -> bool }`, which builds the `deferred` closure from `self.state.introspect_pending_dir().join(format!("job-{id}.json")).exists()` (use `event_key` for the name) and passes `crate::now()`. Add a small `fn review_limit_s(&self, head: &str) -> u64` (`JobConfig::at(&self.git, head)` then `config.budget.reader_timeout_s`, 0 when the config cannot be read). Add unit tests `failure_review_pending_*` with `blank_record()` (introspect.rs:2227).

Step 2, reading.rs (guard): add `pub(crate) fn live_retry_of(records, job: &str) -> Option<(String, JobState)>` (scan `job_history`, keep Queued, Proposed, Blocked or Dispatched, newest first). Add `enum Blocker { Interrupted, Standing, ReviewPending }` with the refusal and override texts, `struct HandGuard { force, jobs, interrupted_job: Option<JobId>, limit_s, planned: Option<Intervention> }`, `Athena::hand_blocker(&self, g, records)` (order: interrupted, then per job standing, then pending), and `Athena::settle_hand(&self, g: &mut HandGuard, records)`. Without force and with a blocker, `settle_hand` bails with the text ending 'Nothing was queued'. With force and a blocker, it builds the Intervention (unique id via `has_record_id`, OverrodeDecision, Observed, class from `job.class()` or 'unknown'). Add `Athena::commit_hand(&self, g, files, subject, body, job)`: `commit_records_with(&|head| g.files_at(self, head, &files), &message(.., trailers))`. `files_at` loads `Records::load(&self.git, head)`; if no override was planned and not forced it runs `hand_blocker` and bails when something blocks; if an override was planned it appends `NewFile::record(&AnyRecord::Intervention(..))`. The trailers are `Athena-Job` and, with an override, `Athena-Intervention`.

Step 3, reading.rs (entry points): rename the body of `first_reading` to `first_reading_with(.., guard: Option<&HandGuard>)` with `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`. With None it calls `self.commit_records(..)` exactly as now; with Some it calls `commit_hand`. `first_reading` calls it with None. Split `ask` into `ask_inner(text, ui, guard)` (ask = None). Split `queue` into `queue_inner(text, guard)` (queue = None; the Some branch commits through `commit_hand`). Split `retry` into `retry_inner(job_ref, hand: Option<bool>, ui) -> Result<(Proposal, bool, Option<RecordId>)>`. For the hand case, after the pause check and `registry().reap()`, compute `retry_target` once, build the guard for `[id, target]`, run `settle_hand`, and skip the old interrupted block (the guard covers it, with the same message). For None keep that block as is. Pass the guard to `ask_inner`, then run `introspect_intervention` when an override was committed. Add `pub fn retry_by_hand(&self, job_ref, force, ui) -> Result<(Proposal, bool, Option<RecordId>)>`. Add `pub fn ask_by_hand(&self, text, force, ui) -> Result<(Proposal, Option<RecordId>)>` and `pub fn queue_by_hand(&self, text, force) -> Result<(JobId, String, Option<RecordId>)>`: load records at head, `retried_job(&records, text)`; for non-retry text call plain `ask` or `queue`; otherwise build the guard for that job, `settle_hand`, then the inner function. Update the doc comments.

Step 4, status.rs and display.rs: add `failure_note: Option<String>` (skip when None, with a doc comment) to `JobLine`; set None in `job_line`. Add the pure `failure_note_text(live: Option<(String, JobState, bool)>, pending: bool) -> Option<String>` and `Athena::failure_note(&self, records, job, limit_s)`. Fill it in `scan_jobs` for Closed(Rejected, Failed, TimedOut, Stale) jobs, computing `limit_s` once with `review_limit_s`. risks.risk: The refactor of `retry`, `ask`, `queue` and `first_reading` into wrappers changes the automatic path by mistake.
risks.mitigation: The wrappers pass None, and the None branch is the old statement (`self.commit_records(..)`). Public signatures are unchanged. The full suite runs, including about 70 retry and ask callers, the drain tests and the run tests.

risks.risk: The pending rule's time bound is a heuristic: a review whose process died stays 'pending' until `reader_timeout_s` (86400 s in the live config) has passed since the outcome, so `athena retry` needs `--force` for up to a day.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text names `--force` and `athena start` as the ways out. The bound is the longest the review's model call may run (introspect.rs:1965), so no running review is missed. CHANGELOG.md states it. After the bound, the job retries as before.

risks.risk: A refused read at commit time loses the reader's spend (no invocation record).
risks.mitigation: This is the same as any commit failure today (gate refusal, commits.rs:203-213). The Err says the reading was discarded. The first check runs before any model call, so the loss happens only in the rare race. Stated in CHANGELOG.md.

risks.risk: A hand retry that commits before the drain's retry does not stop the drain's copy, since the automatic path must not change.
risks.mitigation: A stated limit in CHANGELOG.md. The hand retry sees the drain's retry whenever it commits first, which is the common order because the drain starts right after `go`.

risks.risk: `--force` with a blocker that appears only at commit time goes through with no intervention.
risks.mitigation: A documented exit (e) in the exit table and in CHANGELOG.md. The trailer has to be fixed before the commit, and the user chose the override without seeing that blocker.

risks.risk: The binary test needs `open(true)` to work in the fixture without a real model.
risks.mitigation: The refusal comes before any model call, and tests/introspection.rs:285-307 runs `athena audit` and `athena status` in the same way. If `open` needs something the fixture lacks, the producer replaces the binary case with the method-level case plus the clap parse test and says so in its report.

risks.risk: Status (worktree records) and a hand command (HEAD) disagree for a moment.
risks.mitigation: They are the same commit in normal use. The note is informational; the guard reads HEAD under the commit lock.

risks.risk: The brief lists steward.rs and athena-data records/core.rs as expected deliverables, which this plan does not edit, and adds introspect.rs, display.rs and README.md, which it does not list.
risks.mitigation: The reasons are in the scope decision: steward.rs is the automatic path, the Intervention record needs no change, and the added files carry the pending rule, the display of the new field and the command docs. The verifier checks the diff against the criteria.

demonstrations.fails_without: A diff touching drain.rs or steward.rs, or changing what `Athena::retry` does without a guard, would show in the stat. The drain and run tests would fail if automatic retry changed.
demonstrations.seam: Not a behavior criterion; the evidence is the diff and the existing drain, lifecycle and run tests, which call `Athena::retry` and `ask` without a guard.

demonstrations.method: Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` on the final tree. Also `cargo test -p athena-cli --test retry`, `cargo test -p athena-core failure_note`, `cargo test -p athena-core failure_review_pending` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`. The budgets test is unaffected because no prompt, brief or context file changes. Clippy watch points: `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on `first_reading_with`, and every new struct field used.
demonstrations.fails_without: A new field missing from the `JobLine` literals in display.rs tests (:2679, :2770) breaks the build. Unformatted code or a clippy warning fails the checks.
demonstrations.seam: No new seam; cargo drives the checks.
